newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares up, but correction possible.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares up, but correction possible.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.63 percent on Tuesday on low turnover due to a general reluctance to sell actively, traders said.

"Nobody wants to sell because prices are on the rise. But that may not be the right tactics as it seems to me prices are already very high and may not grow much further," said Karmen Cerar, a trader of brokerage Poteza.
Since January 7, shares have risen over 16 percent.
"As long as the feeling on the market is this positive, the upward trend will continue but a technical correction can't be ruled out," Cerar said.
The SBI index rose 8.47 points to 1,345.9. Eight shares rose, six fell, and 11 were untraded. Turnover fell to 181.3 million tolars from 385.3 million.
Issue A of drug company Lek was the most actively traded, closing 2.67 percent higher at 27,640 tolars on volume of 3,760 shares for total turnover of 103.8 million tolars.
Warehousing company BTC was the top gainer, surging 10.42 percent to 10,490 on volume of 319 shares for total turnover of 3.3 million tolars.
"BTC is a profitable company and the amount of shares on offer is small. Still, today's volume was not big and I doubt this price will keep," said Mateja Gubanec of bank A banka.
Brokerage Nika was the leading decliner falling 2.44 percent to 4,000 on volume of 125 shares for total turnover of 0.5 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana Newsroom, 386-61-126-3644
